name: installments
answer: No, a higher installment count does not reliably mean a higher order value. While some higher installment counts (e.g., 8, 10, 20, 24) show higher average order values, many others (e.g., 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18) have lower averages than lower installment counts, indicating no consistent positive relationship.

evidence.sql:
SELECT payment_installments AS installments,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count,
       ROUND(AVG(order_value), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM orders
WHERE payment_installments IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY payment_installments
ORDER BY payment_installments;

name: delivery_stats
answer: The delivery times range from a minimum of 1.02 days to a maximum of 99.66 days, with an average delivery time of 12.44 days.

evidence.sql:
SELECT MIN(delivery_days) AS min_delivery_days,
       MAX(delivery_days) AS max_delivery_days,
       ROUND(AVG(delivery_days),2) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM orders
WHERE delivery_days >= 0;
